subject: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for confirming our booth placement for TechPlaza Summit. We want to finalise the lead ingestion approach so ops can test before show day. Proposed approach:

- Dual capture: badge scan + optional QR webform. Scans should create/append a contact and add a "captured_via" tag (badge|qr).
- Consent: explicit checkbox text on the webform and a short opt-in banner on the scanner app. Copy suggestions are in the attached "consent-snippets.docx".
- CRM write: primary sync to HubSpot; fallback to SFDc for legacy accounts. We need the field mapping for company, title, email, consent, timestamp, and source.
- Offline mode: scanner must queue payloads and include originating device id + local timestamp; server will reconcile by event_id and email to dedupe.

Can you confirm the file format you expect from the scanner vendor (CSV/JSON) and whether CoreEvents will provide a webhook for immediate posting? Also looping Devon (leadcapture) for device-side details.

Goal: have a tested end-to-end ingest by Mon 2/22 so we can run a dry-run.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon@leadcapture.co>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

Hi Jordan —

Great summary. CoreEvents can provide both a streaming webhook and end-of-day batch CSV from our aggregation pipeline. The scanner vendor (LeadCapture Co) supports JSON POSTs over HTTPS and creates a signed payload for integrity. Devon — can you confirm the device id and offline queuing behavior?

We prefer HubSpot as the primary sink; we can map to Salesforce where HubSpot records fail to match our partner accounts. We can also add an "event_consent" boolean column to the CSV.

Samantha
Operations Manager, CoreEvents
From: Devon Lee <devon@leadcapture.co>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

On Mon, Feb 14, 2027 at 10:03 AM Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com> wrote:
> Great summary. CoreEvents can provide both a streaming webhook and end-of-day batch CSV from our aggregation pipeline.

Quick details from the device side:
- Primary: POST JSON to your webhook with schema v3 (see sample in the drive link).
- Offline: devices store up to 5K events, sign them, and push on reconnect; each record has device_id, local_ts, sequence_no.
- Attachments: images (badge photo) are referenced as s3 URLs (we will not push binaries in handshake).

We recommend the server perform idempotency by (event_id, device_id) and then dedupe by email+timestamp within 5s window. We will include a dedupe key field if you want.

—Devon
LeadCapture Co
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>, Devon Lee <devon@leadcapture.co>, hs-admin@acme-co.com
Date: 2027-02-15T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

Thanks team — I put together a field map and a short workflow in the attached "event-data-mapping-v2.xlsx". Key notes:
- HubSpot mapping: contact.email -> email, contact.full_name -> firstname+lastname split, contact.company -> company, consent_event -> opt_in_source (yes/no), captured_via -> property 'lead_source_detail'.
- SalesForce fallback: create Lead with origin = TradeShow, use external_id = event_id for idempotency.
- Ownership: set owner to the on-floor AE (lookup by booth code) if email domain matches a target account; otherwise set to marketing@redwood.ai.
- Timestamps: prefer server_ingest_ts for sorting; local_ts should be preserved as raw_device_ts in properties.
- GDPR: if consent_event=false and region=eu, mark contact as DO_NOT_CONTACT and block sync to downstream enrichment.

Action items for devs: 1) confirm webhook schema acceptance, 2) confirm HubSpot workflow ID for ingestion (hs-admin can provide), 3) approval on consent copy.

Ben
Field Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>
Date: 2027-02-16T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

Jordan / Ben / Samantha —

I updated consent language in the attached doc with two short variants: one for the QR microform and one for the scanner UI. My recommendation (for legal) is to use the QR copy exactly and the scanner UI to show a short banner "By scanning, you consent to receive emails from Redwood Inference about related products and events." and link to a full PDP.

Example QR checkbox: "Yes — I agree to receive event updates and product information from Redwood Inference. I understand I can unsubscribe at any time."

If we get sign-off, I'll push these copies into the dry-run build and seed HubSpot with the "consent_source" property so we can filter downstream.

—Marissa
Event Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@coreevents.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, hs-admin@acme-co.com
Date: 2027-02-17T15:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid badge + QR leadflow: consent language and CRM sync plan

Thanks everyone — this looks good. Next steps:

1) Devon / LeadCapture to send sample signed JSON payloads to our staging webhook by EOD 2/18.
2) hs-admin to share HubSpot ingestion workflow ID and API key vault path (cc'd).
3) Marissa to lock consent copy and we will deploy to the scanner test image.
4) Ben to own reconciliation logic and run the dry-run ingestion on 2/22; we'll monitor in Console and check the token-level latency/cost dashboard for spike risk.

If there are no blockers I will schedule a 30-min dry-run check on 2/22 10:00am PST.

Jordan
Head of Field Marketing
Redwood Inference
